notes: Truth: a statement title about a hypothetical needs the thought-experiment cue. Here the ringed sky gives it, and the description's first line must say 'A thought experiment'. The rings beat ends 'Tonight's Moon is fine' (c2). The ring is shown thin and in Earth's equatorial plane (c27).
chatgptPrompt:
Create a YouTube thumbnail, 16:9 (1920x1080).
Subject: a calm beach at night with NO Moon in the sky. Instead, one bright, thin silver ring arcs across the whole sky from the left horizon to the right horizon, high over the sea, the way Saturn's rings would look from below. One small person stands alone on the wet sand, looking up at it.
Composition: wide shot. The ring arc spans the full width and peaks in the upper third. The person is tiny and silhouetted at the lower right third. A calm sea in the lower third reflects the ring. Lots of dark sky.
Lighting and treatment: deep indigo night sky (#1B1640 fading to #0B0A1F), the ring glowing silver-white with a faint teal (#3FE0C5) edge, a few stars, soft silver light on the wet sand and water. Quiet, cinematic, very clean, violet (#5B3FD0) undertone.
Mood: quiet awe with a chill: where did the Moon go?
Text: "WHERE'S THE MOON?" in bold white sans-serif, upper left, medium size. No other text.
Scientific accuracy: the ring is one thin, flat band of rock and dust in Earth's equatorial plane, seen as a single arc. No Moon anywhere in the frame, no other planets or moons.
Avoid: no arrows, circles, faces with exaggerated expressions, logos, watermarks, brand names, extra text, NASA-style captions, explosions, meteors hitting Earth, or anything that looks like a real photograph or a news image.
Style: premium editorial science documentary, distinctive and art-directed, not generic AI art.
